_comment: FROZEN capture of the LLM advisory layer. The reviewer is Claude Code itself (an agent), NOT a paid API call -- so this layer is NOT script-reproducible: re-running spawns a fresh agent whose wording varies. We freeze the captured output + the method so the record is auditable. The runner treats this file as a fixed input and does not regenerate it.
_scoring_caveat: Each concern's 'addresses_gt' is SELF-DECLARED by the same analyst who wrote ground_truth.json; the runner credits the LLM via these tags without independently re-matching message text to GT. So the LLM 'coverage' number is SELF-ATTESTED, not independently adjudicated, and the reviewer is non-reproducible. Treat it as a captured claim, not a measured recall. Independent adjudication (a blind matcher) is future work (plan P2 / C3).

method.reviewer: Claude Code agent (Opus 4.x), spawned with fresh/independent context
method.independence_note: Deliberately spawned WITHOUT the main conversation's prior (abstract-based) analysis, to avoid confirmation bias -- the prompt described the audit METHOD, not the expected findings. This is the session's 'independent adversarial reviewer' discipline.

verdict_quote: Not publication-grade. It is a cross-sectional study marketed as future-onset 'prediction', and its flagship diabetes result is circular -- FBG/insulin/HbA1c both define and predict diabetes, so DM AUC ~0.95-0.97 reflects definition leakage, not a useful tool.

concerns.message: Diabetes model is circular: DM is defined by HbA1c>6.5%, and HbA1c/insulin (+FBG via GLM7) are top predictors. DM AUC 0.95-0.97 and HbA1c-alone 0.881 are the leakage signature.
concerns.novelty_vs_rag: synthesized (ties the paper's own DM definition to its feature list and the AUC gradient; not a verbatim KB copy)

concerns.message: Explicitly cross-sectional ('26 289 individuals ... cross-sectional investigation') yet claims future onset / prediction / prognosis. All NHANES cases are prevalent, not incident.

Feature/threshold selection (univariate AUC ranking, 7-factor GLM7 refinement) done on the full dataset before the 0.7:0.3 split -> selection leakage. Also found an 'ElasticNet ... superior' sentence embedded in the XGBoost section -- a likely copy-paste/reproducibility red flag.
concerns.novelty_vs_rag: synthesized + NEW (the ElasticNet/XGBoost copy-paste artifact is not in any KB concern; pure full-text catch)

concerns.message: CHARLS 'external validation' reports both a training and a validation AUROC within CHARLS (model re-fit inside the external cohort); liver AUC drops 0.89->0.73 -> dataset-specific, not transported.
concerns.novelty_vs_rag: synthesized (corrects the over-generous 'clean external cohort' read)

concerns.message: No calibration, no DCA results (despite rmda mentioned), no CIs on the XGBoost AUROCs. Discrimination-only cannot support the clinical-use claim.
concerns.novelty_vs_rag: copy_from_rag-adjacent (echoes PR-002-C01 family but adds the missing-DCA-despite-rmda specific)

concerns.message: BUN and creatinine (CKD definition variables) are predictors of the comorbidity outcome that includes 'failing kidneys'.
